significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) law plus a form-(ii) causal mechanism: per-item "required depth" and the "required-depth deficit" scale with typological/script distance and resource level, predict cross-lingual errors, and selective extra depth recovers errors caused by truncated computation rather than absent knowledge. This would constrain expected layerwise trajectories, error attribution, and the effect of added inference compute across factual recall, reasoning, and translation, while discriminating a depth-budget account from latent-language and representation-conversion explanations studied in work such as Wendler et al., "Do Llamas Work in English?" (ACL 2024). It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanistic account; verified false, especially if distance fails to predict depth or added depth fails selectively, would determinately rule out the proposed fixed-depth bottleneck as an important explanation rather than merely report a missing representation. Topic substitution fails: multilingual representation alone would not earn this score; the claim-specific scaling relation and selective causal recovery are what place it above the topic-median hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handles are the per-item "required depth," the "Truncation Gap," and "adaptive per-item depth allocation" using "looping the final transformer layers" as an intervention. These are potentially ex ante because the claim says deployment teams could "route only high-required-depth items to extra compute," leaving an action window before the final answer is emitted rather than merely explaining an error afterward. After per-model re-extraction, the hypothesis predicts a transferable ordering—greater depth deficits with typological/script distance and lower resource level—and selective recovery, with asserted scope across model families, factual QA, reasoning, and translation; downstream users include teams that route and ship multilingual systems. Topic substitution again fails: the broad multilingual topic supplies none of this routing handle or cross-model predictive relation, although dependence on recalibrated internal trajectories and late-layer looping keeps the reach below a universal deployment rule.
